description: Color-indexed elevation maps for western Alaska is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by National Weather Service | Alaska Region; Alaska Department of Natural Resources, Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys. When an extreme storm is forecast for coastal Alaska, local community leaders and emergency managers wonder "How high will floodwaters reach?" and "Where are negative impacts most likely to occur?" These maps give community leaders and emergency managers a common and clear reference to communicate with one another and with the National Weather Service. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Flooding – Coastal. Assets: Critical Facilities, Natural Areas and Wildlife, Property, Water Infrastructure – Stormwater. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
